QuestionStmt.S: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} [x^2] - [-x^2], & x \neq 3 \\ k, & x = 3 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 3$, then $k =$ where $[\cdot]$ is greatest integer function

Solution.S:
$$\lim_{x \to 3^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^-} ([x^2] - [-x^2]) = 17$$

$$\lim_{x \to 3^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^+} ([x^2] - [-x^2]) = 19$$

Since the left-hand limit and right-hand limit are not equal, $\lim_{x \to 3} f(x)$ does not exist.

Therefore, the function cannot be made continuous at $x = 3$ for any value of $k$. Hence the correct option is D: Does not exist.
